hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases steady-state level y (positive static gain).
With u=0, level y decays over time toward a low level due to self-drain rather than holding constant.
Response to a step in u has lag/delay of several seconds, not instantaneous.
There is a dead-zone at low u where u below ~0.2 produces negligible rise compared to noise.
Steady-state response is roughly monotonic/near-linear and holding y=0.6 requires an intermediate u in ~0.3-0.7, not saturation at 0 or 1.
Sensor noise on y is small relative to the 0.10 control band (std <0.02), so multi-second averaging reveals true level.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Magnitude of static gain and lag/delay at a moderate input, which determines what u is needed to approach the 0.6 target and how fast to actuate.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case conservative rise ignoring drain and lag is 0.2097 + 0.10*0.4*15 = 0.8097, which stays below the 0.85 soft limit with margin, so hard cutoff at 0.9 will not be reached.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive gain with lag is correct, y will rise gradually from ~0.21 toward ~0.35-0.55 over 15s with small noisy fluctuations, staying well below 0.85.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero completed experiments so gain magnitude, lag, zero-decay rate, dead-zone, linearity, hold-input for 0.6, and noise are all unresolved; at least three bounded experiments are required before a controller can be justified.
proposal.operator_note: First probe: holding 40% pump for 15 seconds to measure fill rate and lag.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases steady-state level y (positive static gain).
With u=0, level y decays over time toward near-zero due to self-drain rather than holding constant.
Response to a step in u has lag/delay of ~1-3s, not instantaneous.
Net inflow at low u=0.4 is small, holding y~0.18-0.20 vs ~0.02 at u=0, indicating low effective gain/threshold at low u but not a complete dead-zone at 0.4.
Steady-state y is monotonic in u and holding y=0.6 requires u~0.6-0.9, not u<=0.4.
Sensor noise on y is small relative to the 0.10 control band (std <0.02), so multi-second averaging reveals true level.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain at intermediate-high u and input needed to hold 0.6, which directly determines controller bias/feedforward and whether target is reachable without saturation.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drain or lag is current y 0.021 + 0.10*0.6*12.0 = 0.741, which stays below the 0.85 soft limit.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive gain with 1-2s lag is right, y will stay near 0.02 for ~1-2s then rise gradually toward ~0.25-0.40 over 12s at ~0.02-0.03/s with +/-0.01 noise, staying well below 0.85; flat near 0.02 would imply dead-zone above 0.6, fast jump above 0.5 would imply much higher gain.
proposal.readiness_justification: Gain direction, strong drain at u=0, ~1-2s lag, and small noise are resolved by E1-E3, but steady-state u needed to hold 0.6 and linearity between 0.4 and 0.8 are not yet bracketed because E1 held only ~0.19 and E2 never settled from ~0.39; one intermediate-high hold is needed before controller design is justified.
proposal.operator_note: Pumping at 0.6 for 12s from near-empty to measure climb toward target and pin down hold effort.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases steady-state level y (positive static gain).
With u=0, level y decays over time toward near-zero due to self-drain rather than holding constant.
Response to a step in u has lag/delay of ~1-2s, not instantaneous.
Effective gain is highly nonlinear: large jump from u=0.4 holding y~0.18-0.20 to u=0.5 holding y~0.588, then shallow between 0.5 and 0.6, with no hard dead-zone above 0.4.

Steady-state y is broadly monotonic in u and holding y=0.6 requires u~0.50-0.65; u=0.5 holds ~0.588 over 5s and u=0.55 holds ~0.583 over 4s and u=0.6 holds ~0.589 rising to ~0.595 over 4s and u=0.8 equilibrium is above 0.56 because net inflow is still positive at y~0.5.
Sensor noise on y is small relative to the 0.10 control band (std <0.02, typically <0.01), so multi-second averaging reveals true level.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Precise steady-state input to hold 0.6 and local incremental gain 0.6-0.65, which determines controller bias/feedforward and integral authority to eliminate steady error without overshoot.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound with no drainage: 0.5923 + 0.10*0.65*3.0 = 0.7873 stays below soft limit 0.85; true rate observed ~0.02/s implies actual ~0.62.
proposal.expected_observation: If hold-u ~0.5-0.6 with small local gain and ~1-2s lag is right, y will hold near 0.59 for ~1s then rise at ~0.005-0.015/s toward ~0.61-0.64 over 3s with +/-0.01 noise, staying below 0.70; flat near 0.59 would imply saturated pump / hold-u >=0.65, jump above 0.70 would imply much higher local gain.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction of gain, self-drain to near-zero, 1-2s lag, and small noise are resolved well enough for control, but precise hold-u for 0.6 (0.5 vs 0.55 vs 0.6 vs 0.65) and local incremental gain 0.6-0.65 remain uncertain at ~0.02 level after only 4-5s holds, and that bias directly sets feedforward to reach target without overshoot, so one short bounded probe is warranted and affordable with 3 experiments left.
proposal.operator_note: Probing slightly higher pump for 3s to pin down the effort needed to hold 0.6.
